findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 translated into Italian instead of Lithuanian
findings.body: The value of totpStep1 was changed from a valid Lithuanian sentence containing FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags to Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see a message in the wrong language. The new value is also identical to the login theme's loginTotpStep1, suggesting the author copy-pasted the wrong source translation.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 translated into Italian instead of Lithuanian
findings.body: The value of loginTotpStep1 was changed from a valid Lithuanian sentence containing FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags to Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see a login message in the wrong language.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException for IO errors
findings.body: When the properties file cannot be read, verifySafeHtml throws a plain RuntimeException. The enclosing verify() method declares throws MojoExecutionException and the sibling verifyNoDuplicateKeys uses MojoExecutionException. A RuntimeException here causes the Maven build to fail with a confusing stack trace instead of the standard 'MojoExecutionException: Can not read file ...' error, and it bypasses Mojo error reporting. The same problem exists on line 79 for the English file.

findings.title: PolicyFactory and HTML_TAGS Pattern are instance fields but immutable
findings.body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML, and HTML_TAGS are declared as instance fields but are created from constants (no per-instance state). They should be static to avoid rebuilding the OWASP PolicyFactory and compiling the regex for every VerifyMessageProperties instance. The ANCHOR_PATTERN on line 145 is correctly static; the others should be too.

findings.title: Typo in method name santizeAnchors
findings.body: The helper method is named 'santizeAnchors' (missing the 'i'). It should be 'sanitizeAnchors' to be consistent with the other spelling in the same class (sanitized, sanitize). This is a public-ish helper used from verifySafeHtml and is easy to fix before merge.

findings.title: verifyDuplicateKeysDetected assertion relaxed from contains to hasItem
findings.body: The duplicate-key test was changed from 'Matchers.contains(...)' (exact list match) to 'Matchers.hasItem(...)' (only checks one item is present). This is a regression in test strictness: additional error messages for the same key (e.g., a future Illegal HTML detection on the same fixture) would no longer cause the test to fail, masking real regressions. The original stricter assertion should be retained, possibly by asserting the list size or by separating the duplicate-key case into its own fixture.
